description: Observability of a public transit system from GTFS Realtime: feed health, street operations and service reliability, on the MBTA public feeds read live by DuckDB.

options.content:
### Public transit observability with GTFS Realtime

A demo on the public feed of the **MBTA** (Boston), on three levels: **feed health** — is the data arriving, and on time? —, **street operations** — where are the vehicles, and which ones are running bunched? — and **service reliability** — is the scheduled headway being kept?

The filters at the top — **mode, route, status and occupancy** — apply across the whole dashboard: the map filters instantly, and the tables, stats and subway history recompute (status and occupancy only apply to vehicles; feed age is not filtered).

Everything is queried live with DuckDB, with no intermediate database: the GTFS-RT JSON feeds go through a 15 s cache (the MBTA asks for no more than one request every 10 s) and the history comes from the daily Parquet files of **LAMP**, the MBTA's performance archive. Freshness thresholds follow GTFS Realtime best practices (data younger than 90 s).

<small>Data: Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority, under the MassDOT Developers License Agreement. Independent dashboard, not affiliated with the MBTA.</small>

panels.description: Feed age: seconds since the timestamp in the feed header (includes up to 15 s of caching). Green up to 60 s, amber up to 90 s, red beyond: GTFS Realtime best practices ask for data younger than 90 s. Positions older than 90 s: vehicles whose last report trails the header by more than that. Predictions without a vehicle: trips with estimated times but no vehicle assigned — normal for future departures, suspicious if it grows at rush hour.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

-- MATERIALIZED so each feed is read once per query: the proxy refreshes its
-- copy every 15 s, and a second read landing after a refresh fails DuckDB's
-- ETag check.
WITH vp AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT header, unnest(entity) AS e FROM read_json('http://sources-data/mbta/realtime/VehiclePositions_enhanced.json', maximum_object_size = 50000000)),
     tu AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT header, unnest(entity) AS e FROM read_json('http://sources-data/mbta/realtime/TripUpdates_enhanced.json', maximum_object_size = 50000000)),
-- Vehicle counts follow all four filters, trip counts mode and route (a trip
-- has no status or occupancy). The feed's age is about the feed, so it reads
-- the unfiltered header.
v AS (SELECT header, e FROM vp WHERE CASE
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Subway'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'CR-%'   THEN 'Commuter rail'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Boat-%' THEN 'Ferry'
    ELSE 'Bus'
  END IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR e.vehicle.trip.route_id IN ($route))
    AND CASE e.vehicle.current_status
    WHEN 'IN_TRANSIT_TO' THEN 'In transit'
    WHEN 'STOPPED_AT'    THEN 'Stopped at stop'
    WHEN 'INCOMING_AT'   THEN 'Arriving at stop'
    ELSE 'No data'
  END IN ($status)
    AND CASE e.vehicle.occupancy_status
    WHEN 'EMPTY'                      THEN 'Empty'
    WHEN 'MANY_SEATS_AVAILABLE'       THEN 'Many seats'
    WHEN 'FEW_SEATS_AVAILABLE'        THEN 'Few seats'
    WHEN 'STANDING_ROOM_ONLY'         THEN 'Standing room only'
    WHEN 'CRUSHED_STANDING_ROOM_ONLY' THEN 'Crushed'
    WHEN 'FULL'                       THEN 'Full'
    WHEN 'NOT_ACCEPTING_PASSENGERS'   THEN 'Not accepting passengers'
    ELSE 'No data'
  END IN ($occupancy)),
t AS (SELECT header, e FROM tu WHERE CASE
    WHEN e.trip_update.trip.route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR e.trip_update.trip.route_id LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Subway'
    WHEN e.trip_update.trip.route_id LIKE 'CR-%'   THEN 'Commuter rail'
    WHEN e.trip_update.trip.route_id LIKE 'Boat-%' THEN 'Ferry'
    ELSE 'Bus'
  END IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR e.trip_update.trip.route_id IN ($route)))
SELECT
  (SELECT (epoch(now()) - max(header.timestamp))::BIGINT FROM vp)                          AS "Feed age",
  (SELECT count(*)::BIGINT FROM v)                                                         AS "Vehicles reporting",
  (SELECT round(100.0 * avg((header.timestamp - e.vehicle.timestamp > 90)::INT), 1) FROM v)  AS "Positions older than 90 s",
  (SELECT count(*)::BIGINT FROM t)                                                         AS "Trips with predictions",
  (SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.trip_update.trip.schedule_relationship = 'CANCELED')::BIGINT FROM t) AS "Canceled trips",
  (SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.trip_update.trip.schedule_relationship = 'ADDED')::BIGINT FROM t)    AS "Added trips",
  (SELECT round(100.0 * avg((e.trip_update.vehicle.id IS NULL)::INT), 1) FROM t)           AS "Predictions without a vehicle"

panels.title: Is the data arriving, and on time?

panels.description: Each bus icon is a vehicle from the latest vehicle positions feed, turned to the heading it reports (one that reports none stands upright). Green: reported 30 s ago or less; amber: up to 90 s; red: longer — a vehicle the system believes is in service but that stopped reporting. Click a vehicle to see its next stops in the table on the right. Picking a row in the bunched buses table zooms the map to that pair and marks it with two rings that follow those buses on every refresh.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

-- `vehicle`, not `vehicle_id`: the panel reads vehicle_id as a trajectory id
-- and would try to draw trips. No time column either, so this stays a snapshot.
-- Deliberately unfiltered: the map narrows itself through kepler filters bound
-- to the mode/route/status/occupancy variables, so a selection redraws at once
-- and widening it again needs no new query.
WITH vp AS (SELECT header, unnest(entity) AS e FROM read_json('http://sources-data/mbta/realtime/VehiclePositions_enhanced.json', maximum_object_size = 50000000))
SELECT
  e.vehicle.vehicle.id                AS vehicle,
  e.vehicle.vehicle.label             AS unit,
  e.vehicle.trip.route_id             AS route,
  CASE
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Subway'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'CR-%'   THEN 'Commuter rail'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Boat-%' THEN 'Ferry'
    ELSE 'Bus'
  END                              AS mode,
  e.vehicle.position.bearing::DOUBLE  AS heading,
  e.vehicle.position.latitude         AS latitude,
  e.vehicle.position.longitude        AS longitude,
  CASE e.vehicle.current_status
    WHEN 'IN_TRANSIT_TO' THEN 'In transit'
    WHEN 'STOPPED_AT'    THEN 'Stopped at stop'
    WHEN 'INCOMING_AT'   THEN 'Arriving at stop'
    ELSE 'No data'
  END                            AS status,
  CASE e.vehicle.occupancy_status
    WHEN 'EMPTY'                      THEN 'Empty'
    WHEN 'MANY_SEATS_AVAILABLE'       THEN 'Many seats'
    WHEN 'FEW_SEATS_AVAILABLE'        THEN 'Few seats'
    WHEN 'STANDING_ROOM_ONLY'         THEN 'Standing room only'
    WHEN 'CRUSHED_STANDING_ROOM_ONLY' THEN 'Crushed'
    WHEN 'FULL'                       THEN 'Full'
    WHEN 'NOT_ACCEPTING_PASSENGERS'   THEN 'Not accepting passengers'
    ELSE 'No data'
  END                         AS occupancy,
  (header.timestamp - e.vehicle.timestamp)::BIGINT AS age_s,
  CASE
    WHEN header.timestamp - e.vehicle.timestamp <= 30 THEN '≤ 30 s'
    WHEN header.timestamp - e.vehicle.timestamp <= 90 THEN '30–90 s'
    ELSE '> 90 s'
  END AS freshness
FROM vp

INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

-- The pair picked in the bunching table (variables parA and parB), read live
-- so the rings follow both buses on every refresh. Empty until a row is
-- clicked, which matches nothing.
WITH vp AS (SELECT unnest(entity) AS e FROM read_json('http://sources-data/mbta/realtime/VehiclePositions_enhanced.json', maximum_object_size = 50000000))
SELECT e.vehicle.vehicle.label       AS unit,
       e.vehicle.trip.route_id       AS route,
       e.vehicle.position.latitude   AS latitude,
       e.vehicle.position.longitude  AS longitude
FROM vp
WHERE e.vehicle.vehicle.id IN ($parA, $parB)

panels.description: Pairs of buses on the same route and direction less than 250 m apart. A bus right behind another means a gap behind both: the wait at the next stop grows even with the scheduled fleet on the road. Positions older than 90 s and the first two stops of the route, where buses lay over at the terminal, are left out. Distance: red below 50 m, orange up to 150 m, yellow up to 250 m. Click a row to zoom the map to the pair.

links.title: Zoom the map to this pair

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

-- Two buses of the same route and direction closer than 250 m. Stale
-- positions and the first two stops (terminal layovers) are left out. The
-- pair's midpoint and vehicle ids ride along hidden: the row's data link
-- writes them to lat/lng (the map centres) and parA/parB (the map rings them).
WITH vp AS (SELECT header, unnest(entity) AS e FROM read_json('http://sources-data/mbta/realtime/VehiclePositions_enhanced.json', maximum_object_size = 50000000)),
stops AS (
  -- The archive keeps every version of a stop; the newest name wins. Seven
  -- days back picks the year so the first week of January still finds a file.
  SELECT stop_id, arg_max(stop_name, gtfs_active_date) AS name
  FROM read_parquet('http://sources-data/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/stops.parquet')
  GROUP BY 1
),
bus AS (
  SELECT e.vehicle.vehicle.id          AS id,
         e.vehicle.vehicle.label       AS unit,
         e.vehicle.trip.route_id       AS route,
         e.vehicle.trip.direction_id   AS dir_id,
         e.vehicle.position.latitude   AS lat,
         e.vehicle.position.longitude  AS lon,
         e.vehicle.stop_id             AS stop
  FROM vp
  WHERE header.timestamp - e.vehicle.timestamp <= 90
    AND e.vehicle.current_stop_sequence > 2
    AND CASE
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Subway'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'CR-%'   THEN 'Commuter rail'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Boat-%' THEN 'Ferry'
    ELSE 'Bus'
  END = 'Bus'
    -- Mode and route only: status and occupancy do not make two buses bunched.
    AND CASE
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Subway'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'CR-%'   THEN 'Commuter rail'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Boat-%' THEN 'Ferry'
    ELSE 'Bus'
  END IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR e.vehicle.trip.route_id IN ($route))
),
pairs AS (
  SELECT a.route, a.unit AS a, b.unit AS b, a.id AS id_a, b.id AS id_b, a.stop,
         (a.lat + b.lat) / 2 AS center_lat,
         (a.lon + b.lon) / 2 AS center_lng,
         2 * 6371000 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(b.lat - a.lat) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(a.lat)) * cos(radians(b.lat)) * pow(sin(radians(b.lon - a.lon) / 2), 2))) AS meters
  FROM bus a JOIN bus b ON a.route = b.route AND a.dir_id = b.dir_id AND a.unit < b.unit
)
SELECT p.route                        AS "Route",
       p.a || ' + ' || p.b           AS "Buses",
       coalesce(s.name, p.stop)  AS "Near",
       round(p.meters)::BIGINT       AS "Distance",
       -- Text, not numbers: a data link interpolates the cell's *formatted*
       -- value, and the table's automatic decimals print 42.344533 as 42.3.
       printf('%.6f', p.center_lat)  AS center_lat,
       printf('%.6f', p.center_lng)  AS center_lng,
       p.id_a,
       p.id_b
FROM pairs p LEFT JOIN stops s ON s.stop_id = p.stop
WHERE p.meters < 250
ORDER BY p.meters

panels.description: TripUpdates predictions for the vehicle picked on the map. Empty until the first click.

defaults.noValue: Click a vehicle on the map

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

-- $vehicle is written by a click on the map; empty until then, which
-- matches nothing.
WITH tu AS (SELECT unnest(entity) AS e FROM read_json('http://sources-data/mbta/realtime/TripUpdates_enhanced.json', maximum_object_size = 50000000)),
stops AS (
  -- The archive keeps every version of a stop; the newest name wins. Seven
  -- days back picks the year so the first week of January still finds a file.
  SELECT stop_id, arg_max(stop_name, gtfs_active_date) AS name
  FROM read_parquet('http://sources-data/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/stops.parquet')
  GROUP BY 1
),
upcoming AS (
  SELECT e.trip_update.trip.route_id AS route,
         st.stop_sequence            AS seq,
         st.stop_id                  AS stop,
         coalesce(st.arrival.time, st.departure.time) AS t
  FROM (SELECT e, unnest(e.trip_update.stop_time_update) AS st FROM tu)
  WHERE e.trip_update.vehicle.id = $vehicle
)
SELECT p.route                                         AS "Route",
       coalesce(n.name, p.stop)                   AS "Stop",
       to_timestamp(p.t)                              AS "Estimated arrival",
       round((p.t - epoch(now())) / 60.0)::BIGINT     AS "Due in"
FROM upcoming p LEFT JOIN stops n ON n.stop_id = p.stop
WHERE p.t >= epoch(now()) - 60
ORDER BY p.seq
LIMIT 15

panels.description: Where the stale positions concentrate. At the MBTA it is usually the subway: trains parked in yards stay published.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

WITH vp AS (SELECT header, unnest(entity) AS e FROM read_json('http://sources-data/mbta/realtime/VehiclePositions_enhanced.json', maximum_object_size = 50000000)),
v AS (SELECT CASE
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Subway'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'CR-%'   THEN 'Commuter rail'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Boat-%' THEN 'Ferry'
    ELSE 'Bus'
  END AS mode, header.timestamp - e.vehicle.timestamp AS age FROM vp WHERE CASE
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Subway'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'CR-%'   THEN 'Commuter rail'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Boat-%' THEN 'Ferry'
    ELSE 'Bus'
  END IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR e.vehicle.trip.route_id IN ($route))
    AND CASE e.vehicle.current_status
    WHEN 'IN_TRANSIT_TO' THEN 'In transit'
    WHEN 'STOPPED_AT'    THEN 'Stopped at stop'
    WHEN 'INCOMING_AT'   THEN 'Arriving at stop'
    ELSE 'No data'
  END IN ($status)
    AND CASE e.vehicle.occupancy_status
    WHEN 'EMPTY'                      THEN 'Empty'
    WHEN 'MANY_SEATS_AVAILABLE'       THEN 'Many seats'
    WHEN 'FEW_SEATS_AVAILABLE'        THEN 'Few seats'
    WHEN 'STANDING_ROOM_ONLY'         THEN 'Standing room only'
    WHEN 'CRUSHED_STANDING_ROOM_ONLY' THEN 'Crushed'
    WHEN 'FULL'                       THEN 'Full'
    WHEN 'NOT_ACCEPTING_PASSENGERS'   THEN 'Not accepting passengers'
    ELSE 'No data'
  END IN ($occupancy))
SELECT mode                                     AS "Mode",
       count(*)::BIGINT                         AS "Vehicles",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE age > 90)::BIGINT AS "Positions older than 90 s",
       max(age)::BIGINT                        AS "Oldest position"
FROM v GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.description: Alerts feed: notices in effect right now, grouped by the effect the agency declares.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

WITH al AS (SELECT unnest(entity) AS e FROM read_json('http://sources-data/mbta/realtime/Alerts_enhanced.json', maximum_object_size = 50000000))
SELECT
  CASE e.alert.effect
    WHEN 'NO_SERVICE'          THEN 'No service'
    WHEN 'REDUCED_SERVICE'     THEN 'Reduced service'
    WHEN 'SIGNIFICANT_DELAYS'  THEN 'Significant delays'
    WHEN 'DETOUR'              THEN 'Detour'
    WHEN 'ADDITIONAL_SERVICE'  THEN 'Additional service'
    WHEN 'MODIFIED_SERVICE'    THEN 'Modified service'
    WHEN 'STOP_MOVED'          THEN 'Stop moved'
    WHEN 'ACCESSIBILITY_ISSUE' THEN 'Accessibility'
    WHEN 'OTHER_EFFECT'        THEN 'Other'
    ELSE 'Unknown'
  END AS "Effect",
  count(*)::BIGINT AS "Alerts"
FROM al
-- Active now: some period has started and has not ended (no end = open).
WHERE len(list_filter(e.alert.active_period,
          p -> p.start <= epoch(now()) AND coalesce(p."end", 9999999999) >= epoch(now()))) > 0
  -- And it names at least one route inside the mode and route selection.
  AND len(list_filter(e.alert.informed_entity,
          x -> x.route_id IS NOT NULL
               AND CASE
    WHEN x.route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR x.route_id LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Subway'
    WHEN x.route_id LIKE 'CR-%'   THEN 'Commuter rail'
    WHEN x.route_id LIKE 'Boat-%' THEN 'Ferry'
    ELSE 'Bus'
  END IN ($mode)
               AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR x.route_id IN ($route)))) > 0
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Active service alerts
Subway reliability · history (follows the time range up to yesterday, and the mode and route filters)

panels.description: From the MBTA's LAMP archive: every time a train passes a station, with its actual and scheduled headway. Excess wait = expected wait, actual minus scheduled, where expected wait = Σh² / 2Σh (the metric used by the MBTA, TfL and the MTA). Gaps: headways over 1.5 times the schedule. Bunched: under a quarter of it. Minutes.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;

-- One LAMP file per service day in the dashboard range. Capped at 31 days and
-- at yesterday in Boston: today's file may not exist yet, and a missing file
-- fails the whole read. A range inside today still reads yesterday.
WITH d AS (
  -- Branch headways where the station is on a branch (Green-B/C/D/E), trunk
  -- headways otherwise; comparing a branch stop against the trunk schedule
  -- invents gaps. Intervals of an hour or more are the overnight break.
  SELECT trunk_route_id AS line,
         route_id,
         parent_station,
         direction_destination,
         to_timestamp(stop_timestamp) AS t,
         coalesce(headway_branch_seconds, headway_trunk_seconds)     AS h,
         coalesce(scheduled_headway_branch, scheduled_headway_trunk) AS hs
  FROM read_parquet([
  'http://sources-data/mbta/lamp/subway-on-time-performance-v1/' || strftime(d, '%Y-%m-%d') || '-subway-on-time-performance-v1.parquet'
  FOR d IN generate_series(
    least(greatest(CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMPTZ)::DATE, CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMPTZ)::DATE - 30), (now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York')::DATE - 1),
    least(CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMPTZ)::DATE, (now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York')::DATE - 1),
    INTERVAL 1 DAY)
])
),
-- Some rows carry headways but no stop timestamp; a null in the time column
-- makes Grafana's time series report all of its data as out of range.
-- The dashboard's mode and route filters reach the history too. LAMP's route_id
-- uses the live feed's ids (Green-B…E, Red, Orange, Blue, Mattapan), so the same
-- selection applies unchanged; a selection without Subway leaves it empty.
ok AS (
  SELECT * FROM d
  WHERE t IS NOT NULL AND h > 0 AND hs > 0 AND h < 3600 AND hs < 3600
    AND 'Subway' IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route_id IN ($route))
)
SELECT line                                              AS "Line",
       count(*)::BIGINT                                   AS "Samples",
       round(median(h) / 60.0, 1)                         AS "Actual",
       round(median(hs) / 60.0, 1)                        AS "Scheduled",
       -- Excess wait time: a rider's expected wait, Σh²/2Σh, real minus scheduled.
       round((sum(h ^ 2) / (2 * sum(h)) - sum(hs ^ 2) / (2 * sum(hs))) / 60.0, 2)                                    AS "Excess wait",
       round(100.0 * avg((h < 0.25 * hs)::INT), 1)        AS "Bunched",
       round(100.0 * avg((h > 1.5 * hs)::INT), 1)         AS "Gaps"
FROM ok GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;

-- One LAMP file per service day in the dashboard range. Capped at 31 days and
-- at yesterday in Boston: today's file may not exist yet, and a missing file
-- fails the whole read. A range inside today still reads yesterday.
WITH d AS (
  -- Branch headways where the station is on a branch (Green-B/C/D/E), trunk
  -- headways otherwise; comparing a branch stop against the trunk schedule
  -- invents gaps. Intervals of an hour or more are the overnight break.
  SELECT trunk_route_id AS line,
         route_id,
         parent_station,
         direction_destination,
         to_timestamp(stop_timestamp) AS t,
         coalesce(headway_branch_seconds, headway_trunk_seconds)     AS h,
         coalesce(scheduled_headway_branch, scheduled_headway_trunk) AS hs
  FROM read_parquet([
  'http://sources-data/mbta/lamp/subway-on-time-performance-v1/' || strftime(d, '%Y-%m-%d') || '-subway-on-time-performance-v1.parquet'
  FOR d IN generate_series(
    least(greatest(CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMPTZ)::DATE, CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMPTZ)::DATE - 30), (now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York')::DATE - 1),
    least(CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMPTZ)::DATE, (now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York')::DATE - 1),
    INTERVAL 1 DAY)
])
),
-- Some rows carry headways but no stop timestamp; a null in the time column
-- makes Grafana's time series report all of its data as out of range.
-- The dashboard's mode and route filters reach the history too. LAMP's route_id
-- uses the live feed's ids (Green-B…E, Red, Orange, Blue, Mattapan), so the same
-- selection applies unchanged; a selection without Subway leaves it empty.
ok AS (
  SELECT * FROM d
  WHERE t IS NOT NULL AND h > 0 AND hs > 0 AND h < 3600 AND hs < 3600
    AND 'Subway' IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route_id IN ($route))
)
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 HOUR, t) AS time,
       CASE WHEN count(*) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Red') >= 20
         THEN round(100.0 * avg((h > 1.5 * hs)::INT) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Red'), 1) END AS "Red",
       CASE WHEN count(*) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Orange') >= 20
         THEN round(100.0 * avg((h > 1.5 * hs)::INT) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Orange'), 1) END AS "Orange",
       CASE WHEN count(*) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Blue') >= 20
         THEN round(100.0 * avg((h > 1.5 * hs)::INT) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Blue'), 1) END AS "Blue",
       CASE WHEN count(*) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Green') >= 20
         THEN round(100.0 * avg((h > 1.5 * hs)::INT) FILTER (WHERE line = 'Green'), 1) END AS "Green"
FROM ok GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

-- The dashboard's mode and route filters reach the history too. LAMP's route_id
-- uses the live feed's ids (Green-B…E, Red, Orange, Blue, Mattapan), so the same
-- selection applies unchanged; a selection without Subway leaves it empty.
ok AS (
  SELECT * FROM d
  WHERE t IS NOT NULL AND h > 0 AND hs > 0 AND h < 3600 AND hs < 3600
    AND 'Subway' IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route_id IN ($route))
),
stops AS (
  -- The archive keeps every version of a stop; the newest name wins. Seven
  -- days back picks the year so the first week of January still finds a file.
  SELECT stop_id, arg_max(stop_name, gtfs_active_date) AS name
  FROM read_parquet('http://sources-data/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/stops.parquet')
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT o.line                                  AS "Line",
       coalesce(p.name, o.parent_station)     AS "Station",
       o.direction_destination                  AS "Toward",
       count(*)::BIGINT                         AS "Samples",
       round((sum(h ^ 2) / (2 * sum(h)) - sum(hs ^ 2) / (2 * sum(hs))) / 60.0, 1)                          AS "Excess wait",
       round(100.0 * avg((h > 1.5 * hs)::INT), 1) AS "Gaps"
FROM ok o LEFT JOIN stops p ON p.stop_id = o.parent_station
GROUP BY ALL
HAVING count(*) >= 100
ORDER BY "Excess wait" DESC
LIMIT 10

panels.description: Every subway station with at least 100 measured samples in some direction, carrying its worst direction in the range. Color and size grow with the excess wait.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;

-- One LAMP file per service day in the dashboard range. Capped at 31 days and
-- at yesterday in Boston: today's file may not exist yet, and a missing file
-- fails the whole read. A range inside today still reads yesterday.
WITH d AS (
  -- Branch headways where the station is on a branch (Green-B/C/D/E), trunk
  -- headways otherwise; comparing a branch stop against the trunk schedule
  -- invents gaps. Intervals of an hour or more are the overnight break.
  SELECT trunk_route_id AS line,
         route_id,
         parent_station,
         direction_destination,
         to_timestamp(stop_timestamp) AS t,
         coalesce(headway_branch_seconds, headway_trunk_seconds)     AS h,
         coalesce(scheduled_headway_branch, scheduled_headway_trunk) AS hs
  FROM read_parquet([
  'http://sources-data/mbta/lamp/subway-on-time-performance-v1/' || strftime(d, '%Y-%m-%d') || '-subway-on-time-performance-v1.parquet'
  FOR d IN generate_series(
    least(greatest(CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMPTZ)::DATE, CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMPTZ)::DATE - 30), (now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York')::DATE - 1),
    least(CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMPTZ)::DATE, (now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York')::DATE - 1),
    INTERVAL 1 DAY)
])
),
-- Some rows carry headways but no stop timestamp; a null in the time column
-- makes Grafana's time series report all of its data as out of range.
-- The dashboard's mode and route filters reach the history too. LAMP's route_id
-- uses the live feed's ids (Green-B…E, Red, Orange, Blue, Mattapan), so the same
-- selection applies unchanged; a selection without Subway leaves it empty.
ok AS (
  SELECT * FROM d
  WHERE t IS NOT NULL AND h > 0 AND hs > 0 AND h < 3600 AND hs < 3600
    AND 'Subway' IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route_id IN ($route))
),
stops AS (
  SELECT stop_id,
         arg_max(stop_name, gtfs_active_date) AS name,
         arg_max(stop_lat, gtfs_active_date)  AS lat,
         arg_max(stop_lon, gtfs_active_date)  AS lon
  FROM read_parquet('http://sources-data/mbta/lamp/gtfs_archive/' || strftime(current_date - 7, '%Y') || '/stops.parquet')
  GROUP BY 1
),
-- Excess wait per station, line and direction first, as in the table. Pooling
-- the headways of two lines into one Σh² would describe a wait no rider has.
segment AS (
  SELECT parent_station, line, direction_destination AS toward,
         count(*) AS samples,
         (sum(h ^ 2) / (2 * sum(h)) - sum(hs ^ 2) / (2 * sum(hs))) / 60.0 AS ewt,
         100.0 * avg((h > 1.5 * hs)::INT) AS gaps
  FROM ok GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(*) >= 100
),
-- One point per station, carrying its worst direction.
station AS (
  SELECT parent_station,
         string_agg(DISTINCT line, ' / ' ORDER BY line) AS lines,
         sum(samples)::BIGINT                              AS samples,
         max(ewt)                                        AS ewt,
         arg_max(line || ' to ' || toward, ewt)       AS worst_direction,
         arg_max(gaps, ewt)                            AS gaps
  FROM segment GROUP BY 1
)
-- No column called count or direction: the panel reads both as field roles.
SELECT p.name                      AS station,
       e.lines,
       e.worst_direction,
       p.lat                         AS latitude,
       p.lon                         AS longitude,
       e.samples,
       round(e.ewt, 2)               AS excess_wait,
       round(e.gaps, 1)            AS gaps,
       -- Size channel: better-than-scheduled stations come out negative.
       round(greatest(e.ewt, 0), 2)  AS size_weight,
       CASE WHEN e.ewt < 1 THEN '< 1 min' WHEN e.ewt < 2 THEN '1–2 min' ELSE '> 2 min' END AS band
FROM station e JOIN stops p ON p.stop_id = e.parent_station

list.definition:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

-- Variable query: Grafana does not quote variables here as it does in panel
-- queries, so mode is spelled out with the sqlstring format.
SELECT route FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT e.vehicle.trip.route_id AS route, CASE
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Subway'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'CR-%'   THEN 'Commuter rail'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Boat-%' THEN 'Ferry'
    ELSE 'Bus'
  END AS mode
  FROM (SELECT unnest(entity) AS e FROM read_json('http://sources-data/mbta/realtime/VehiclePositions_enhanced.json', maximum_object_size = 50000000))
  WHERE e.vehicle.trip.route_id IS NOT NULL
    AND CASE
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id IN ('Red', 'Orange', 'Blue', 'Mattapan') OR e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Green-%' THEN 'Subway'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'CR-%'   THEN 'Commuter rail'
    WHEN e.vehicle.trip.route_id LIKE 'Boat-%' THEN 'Ferry'
    ELSE 'Bus'
  END IN (${mode:sqlstring})
)
ORDER BY CASE mode WHEN 'Subway' THEN 0 WHEN 'Commuter rail' THEN 1 WHEN 'Ferry' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END,
         try_cast(route AS INTEGER) NULLS LAST, route
